info.title: NaN API
info.description:
Open models on a shared EU inference cluster. Zero logs.

The NaN API is OpenAI-compatible: predictable, resource-oriented URLs, JSON request and response bodies, and standard HTTP verbs and status codes. Point any OpenAI SDK at our base URL and your existing code keeps working. Change the base URL and the API key, and that's it.

One schema across every model, so you only learn the API once. Change the `model` field to switch models; everything else stays the same.

- Base URL: `https://api.nan.builders/v1`
- OpenAPI spec: this document. Import it into Postman, Insomnia, or your own tooling.

If you use the [Helmcode](https://helmcode.com) enterprise service, the base URL is `https://api.helmcode.com/v1` instead. Every other endpoint is identical.

## Authentication

Every request authenticates with an API key, sent as a Bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer $NAN_API_KEY
```

You must be a NaN community member. Generate your key from user settings, under "API Keys", on the [platform](https://cloud.nan.builders/). The key is personal and non-transferable. Keep it secret: never embed one in client-side code or commit it to source control. Requests must go over HTTPS; calls over plain HTTP fail.

## Making requests

The API is OpenAI-compatible, so point an official OpenAI SDK at our base URL and change nothing else:

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="$NAN_API_KEY",
    base_url="https://api.nan.builders/v1",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen3.6",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```

## Streaming

Chat responses can stream token-by-token. Set `"stream": true` on `/chat/completions` and the response arrives as Server-Sent Events: each event is a `data:` line carrying a `chat.completion.chunk`, with the new text in `choices[0].delta.content`. A final `data: [DONE]` line ends the stream. Only `/chat/completions` streams incrementally; `/responses` currently emits a single terminal event.

## Rate limits

{{RATE_LIMITS}}

Web search runs on its own budget, separate from the model endpoints: 20 requests per minute, 3 concurrent, and 500 searches per day per key. Image endpoints have their own too: 20 requests per minute and 100 requests per month. Exceed any limit and you get a `429`.

## Errors

NaN uses conventional HTTP status codes: `2xx` on success, `4xx` for a problem with the request (a missing parameter, an invalid key, an unavailable model) and `5xx` for a server-side error. Every error returns a JSON body in the OpenAI shape:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "The model 'foo' does not exist.",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": "model",
    "code": "model_not_found"
  }
}
```

`message` is human-readable, `param` names the offending field when applicable, and `code` is a short machine-readable string you can branch on.

| Status | Meaning | `code` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | Invalid or malformed parameter (`param` says which); or content blocked by the safety filter. | `invalid_request_error` · `content_policy_violation` |
| `401` | Missing or invalid API key. | `invalid_api_key` |
| `402` | The token allowance for the billing period is spent on a model that carries one, such as `glm5.2`. Not retryable: the counter returns to zero when your billing period starts. | `monthly_cap_reached` |
| `403` | Your tier can't access this endpoint or model. Image generation requires inference membership. | `tier_restricted` |
| `404` | The requested model doesn't exist. | `model_not_found` |
| `429` | Rate limit hit (`rpm_limit`, `max_parallel_requests`), the rolling 4h token budget of `glm5.2`, or a quota exhausted. | `rate_limit_exceeded` · `insufficient_quota` · `quota_exceeded` |
| `500` | Something went wrong on our side (includes upstream model errors). | (none) |
| `503` | Web search is temporarily unavailable; retry shortly. | `search_unavailable` |
| `524` | Timeout, typical with large audio files on `/audio/transcriptions`. | (none) |

Retry `429` and `5xx` responses with exponential backoff. Don't retry `400`, `401`, `403`, or `404` blindly: they'll fail the same way every time until you change the request. `402` cannot be fixed by repetition either: it clears when your billing period starts.

## Model catalog

Every endpoint takes a `model` id. Capabilities vary by model:

| Model | Use for | Capabilities |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deepseek-v4-flash` | Chat, reasoning | Streaming, tool calling, reasoning, 1M-token context. 2B tokens/month per member |
| `mimo-v2.5` | Chat, vision, audio | Streaming, tool calling, reasoning, image input, audio input, 1M-token context. 1.0B tokens/month per member |
| `qwen3.8-flash` | Chat, vision, agents | Streaming, tool calling, reasoning (on by default), vision, 262K-token context. 1B tokens/month per member |
| `glm5.3-flash` | Chat, vision, agents | Streaming, tool calling, reasoning, vision, 1M-token context. 500M tokens/month per member |
| `qwen3.6` | Chat, agents | Streaming, tool calling, vision, reasoning (opt-out, returns `reasoning_content`) |
| `gemma4` | Chat, vision, agents | Streaming, tool calling, vision, reasoning (opt-in) |
| `glm5.2` | Coding, long-horizon agents | Streaming, tool calling, reasoning trace, 500K-token context. Premium tier only |
| `qwen3-embedding` | Embeddings | 4096-dimension vectors |
| `rerank` | RAG reranking | Qwen3-Reranker-8B, 100+ languages |
| `kokoro` | Text-to-speech | Multiple voices and audio formats |
| `whisper` | Speech-to-text | Transcription with word/segment timestamps |
| `flux-2-klein` | Image generation | Text-to-image and image-to-image |

`glm5.2` is served only to keys on the GLM 5.2 premium tier; every other model is available to any inference member. Call [List models](#tag/Models) for the exact set available to your key.

## Versioning & compatibility

The API tracks the OpenAI API surface, so OpenAI SDKs and tools work against `https://api.nan.builders/v1` unchanged. This reference documents the stable public `/v1` endpoints, and we add capabilities without breaking existing fields.

get.description: Returns a list of the models available to your API key, most-capable first. Each entry is a [Model](#tag/Models) object. Use an `id` as the `model` field in your requests.

x-codeSamples.label: cURL
x-codeSamples.source:
curl https://api.nan.builders/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NAN_API_KEY"

x-codeSamples.label: Python
x-codeSamples.source:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="$NAN_API_KEY",
    base_url="https://api.nan.builders/v1",
)

for m in client.models.list().data:
    print(m.id)

post.description: Creates a model response for the given chat conversation. Compatible with OpenAI's Chat Completions API.

model.description:
Model id. See [List models](#tag/Models) for what your key can use. Chat models are `deepseek-v4-flash`, `mimo-v2.5`, `qwen3.8-flash`, `glm5.3-flash`, `qwen3.6`, `gemma4` and `glm5.2`.

`glm5.2` requires a key on the GLM 5.2 premium tier; other keys get `403` `tier_restricted`. The rest are available to every inference member.

messages.description: The conversation so far, oldest first. `content` is a string, or an array of parts (`text` + `image_url`) for vision input on `qwen3.6` and `gemma4`.

max_tokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature. Higher is more random, lower more deterministic.

top_p.description: Nucleus sampling: only consider the top `top_p` probability mass.

stream.description: When `true`, the reply arrives as Server-Sent Events: each `data:` line is a `chat.completion.chunk` with new text in `choices[0].delta.content`, ending with `data: [DONE]`.

tools.description: Functions the model may call (OpenAI function schema). When it calls one, the reply carries `choices[0].message.tool_calls` and `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`. Validated on `qwen3.6`.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning depth (`deepseek-v4-flash` only). The trace comes back in `message.reasoning_content`. More effort helps on hard problems, at the cost of latency and tokens.

chat_template_kwargs.description: Reasoning toggle for `qwen3.6`/`gemma4`: `{ "enable_thinking": boolean }`. In OpenAI SDKs, pass it inside `extra_body`.

premium_tier.description: `glm5.2` is served only to keys on the GLM 5.2 premium tier. Same request shape as any other model, only `model` changes. A key without the tier gets `403` `tier_restricted`.

messages.content: Refactor this function and explain the trade-offs.

200.description: The chat completion. When `stream: false` the body is a single `chat.completion` (`application/json`). When `stream: true` the body is a `text/event-stream` of `chat.completion.chunk` events ending with `data: [DONE]`.

curl https://api.nan.builders/v1/chat/completions \

  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

post.description: Creates an embedding vector representing the input text. Pair with [Rerank](#tag/Rerank) to build a retrieval stack. Model: `qwen3-embedding` (4096-dimension vectors).

input.description: The text to embed: a single string, or an array of strings to embed in one request.

encoding_format.description: The format of the returned vectors: `float` (default) or `base64`.

post.description: Reranks a list of documents by their relevance to a query, returning them ordered most-relevant first. Completes the RAG stack with `qwen3-embedding`: retrieve top-K by embedding similarity, then reorder here. Supports 100+ languages and code. Model: `rerank`. Also available at `/v2/rerank`.

query.description: The query each document is scored against.
query.example: What is the capital of France?

documents.description: The documents to rerank. Returned sorted by descending relevance, each keeping its original `index`.
example: Paris is the capital of France.
Berlin is the capital of Germany.
Madrid is the capital of Spain.

top_n.description: Return only the `top_n` most relevant documents. Defaults to all.

document.text: Paris is the capital of France.
Berlin is the capital of Germany.

x-codeSamples.label: cURL
x-codeSamples.source:
curl https://api.nan.builders/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NAN_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "rerank",
    "query": "What is the capital of France?",
    "documents": ["Paris is the capital of France.", "Berlin is the capital of Germany."]
  }'

x-codeSamples.label: Python
x-codeSamples.source:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="$NAN_API_KEY",
    base_url="https://api.nan.builders/v1",
)

# rerank isn't part of the OpenAI client, so call it directly:
resp = client.post(
    "/rerank",
    cast_to=object,
    body={
        "model": "rerank",
        "query": "What is the capital of France?",
        "documents": ["Paris is the capital of France.", "Berlin is the capital of Germany."],
    },
)
for r in resp["results"]:
    print(r["index"], r["relevance_score"])

post.description:
Transcribes audio into text (speech-to-text). Model: `whisper`. Send the audio as `multipart/form-data`.

Limits: max 25 MB per request. Audio longer than ~2 minutes may time out (`524`); split it into shorter segments. OGG/Opus and MP3 give the best size-to-quality ratio.

language.description: The input language as an ISO-639-1 code (e.g. `es`, `en`). Auto-detected if omitted.

timestamp_granularities[].description: Timestamp detail (with `verbose_json`): `word` fills the `words` array; `segment` (default) fills `segments`.

524.description: Timeout: the audio was too long to transcribe in one request. Split it into segments of 2 minutes or less.

x-codeSamples.label: cURL
x-codeSamples.source:
curl https://api.nan.builders/v1/audio/transcriptions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NAN_API_KEY" \
  -F "model=whisper" \
  -F "file=@audio.mp3"

post.description:
Creates one or more images from a text prompt (text-to-image). Model: `flux-2-klein`.

Requires `inference`-tier membership (`403` otherwise). Image endpoints are rate-limited separately from chat: 20 requests per minute and 100 requests per month per user. These don't consume your chat token budget. `stream: true` is not supported. For OpenAI SDK compatibility, `quality`, `style`, `background`, `moderation`, `output_format`, `output_compression`, and `user` are accepted but ignored.

prompt.description: A text description of the image to generate.
prompt.example: Un faro al atardecer sobre acantilados, estilo cinemático

model.description: The image model. An unknown model returns `404`.

n.description: The number of images to generate (1–4). Values above 4 return `400`.

size.description: "WIDTHxHEIGHT". Each side divisible by 16 and between 256 and 1536, aspect ratio 1:3–3:1. `auto` or omitted → `1024x1024`.

response_format.description: `url` returns a temporary link (~60 min); `b64_json` returns inline base64 bytes.

seed.description: NaN extension: base seed for reproducibility (in OpenAI SDKs, pass via `extra_body`).

guidance.description: NaN extension: FLUX guidance scale (in OpenAI SDKs, pass via `extra_body`).

x-codeSamples.label: cURL
x-codeSamples.source:
curl https://api.nan.builders/v1/images/generations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NAN_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "model": "flux-2-klein", "prompt": "Un faro al atardecer sobre acantilados", "size": "1024x1024" }'

client = OpenAI(

img = client.images.generate(

    prompt="Un faro al atardecer sobre acantilados",

post.description:
Remote [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server, so our tools can be used inside any MCP-compatible agent or client with the same `sk-` key as the REST API.

Transport is streamable HTTP and stateless; the protocol is JSON-RPC 2.0 with the methods `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call` and `ping`. Today the server exposes a single tool, `web_search`, with the same arguments as [Web search](#tag/Search); it is a growing registry, so use `tools/list` to discover the current set.

MCP calls share the **same** per-key rate limit, daily quota and concurrency as the equivalent REST endpoint, so there is no separate budget. A `web_search` tool call over MCP counts exactly like a `POST /v1/search` request.

Note this endpoint lives at the host root, `https://api.nan.builders/mcp`, not under `/v1`.

200.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 response. Protocol-level failures are reported in `error` with HTTP `200`.

x-codeSamples.label: cURL
MCP client config

bearerAuth.description: Personal, non-transferable API key. Send as `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>` on every request.

Model.description: An available model, in the OpenAI-compatible model shape.

id.description: The model's unique slug. Pass this value as the `model` field in your requests.

object.description: The object type, which is always `model`.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the model became available.

owned_by.description: The organization that owns the model.

ContentPart.description: One part of a multimodal message. Use an array of these as `content` for vision input.

url.description: Public URL or `data:` URI of the image.

Message.description: A single message in a conversation. The `role` determines which other fields apply.

role.description: The role of the message author: `system`, `user`, `assistant`, or `tool`.

content.description: The contents of the message. A plain string, or an array of content parts for multimodal input. Can be `null` on an `assistant` message that only returns tool calls.

name.description: An optional name for the author of this message.

tool_calls.description: The tool calls generated by the model. Present on `assistant` messages when the model decides to invoke one or more tools.

tool_call_id.description: The id of the tool call this message answers. Required when `role` is `tool`.

reasoning_content.description: The model's reasoning trace. Present only for reasoning models; safe to display or ignore.

Tool.description: A function the model may call. Provide these in the request's `tools` array.

type.description: The type of the tool. Currently only `function` is supported.

name.description: The name of the function to call. Up to 64 characters; letters, digits, underscores and dashes.

description.description: What the function does, used by the model to decide when and how to call it. Be descriptive.

parameters.description: The parameters the function accepts, described as a JSON Schema object.

ToolChoice.description: Controls tool use: `"auto"` (default), `"none"`, `"required"`, or force one with `{ "type": "function", "function": { "name": "..." } }`.

ToolCall.description: A tool the model chose to call. Execute it, then send the result back in a `tool` message referencing `id`.

id.description: A unique id for this tool call. Pass it as `tool_call_id` in your follow-up `tool` message.

type.description: The type of the tool call. Always `function`.

name.description: The name of the function to call.

arguments.description: The function arguments as a JSON-encoded string. Parse and validate it before use; models can occasionally emit malformed JSON.

ResponseFormat.description: Force structured output. `json_object` guarantees syntactically valid JSON; `json_schema` (with `strict: true`) constrains the output to a schema. Works on `qwen3.6` and `gemma4`.

prompt_tokens.description: The number of tokens in the prompt (input).

completion_tokens.description: The number of tokens in the generated completion (output).

total_tokens.description: The total tokens used: `prompt_tokens` plus `completion_tokens`. This is what counts against your quota.

ChatCompletion.description: The model's response to a chat request. Represents a single, non-streamed completion.

id.description: A unique identifier for the completion.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the completion was created.

model.description: The model that produced the completion.

index.description: The index of this choice in the `choices` array.

finish_reason.description: Why the model stopped: `stop` (natural end or a stop sequence), `length` (hit `max_tokens`), or `tool_calls` (the model called a tool).

choices.description: The list of completion choices. Contains a single choice unless you request more.

ChatCompletionChunk.description: One Server-Sent Event chunk when `stream: true`. New text arrives in `choices[0].delta.content`; the stream ends with `data: [DONE]`.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the chunk was created. Identical across all chunks of one response.

delta.description: The incremental update for this chunk. `role` is set on the first chunk; `content` carries the new text to append.

finish_reason.description: `null` on intermediate chunks; set to the stop reason on the final content chunk.

Error.description: OpenAI-standard error envelope: a non-2xx HTTP status with a JSON body describing the problem.

Embedding.description: A single embedding vector for one input.

index.description: The position of this embedding in the request `input` array.

embedding.description: The embedding vector: a list of 4096 floats. Cosine similarity between vectors measures semantic closeness.

EmbeddingList.description: A list of embeddings, one per input.

model.description: The model used to create the embeddings.

data.description: The embeddings, in the same order as the request `input`.

index.description: The position of this document in the request `documents` array.

relevance_score.description: Relevance to the query, in the range [0, 1]. Higher is more relevant. Results are returned sorted by this, descending.

id.description: A unique identifier for the rerank request.

results.description: The documents, sorted by descending `relevance_score`. Each carries its original `index`.

Transcription.description: A transcription of the supplied audio.

language.description: The detected (or supplied) language, as an ISO-639-1 code.

duration.description: The audio duration in seconds. Present with `verbose_json`.

words.description: Per-word timestamps `[{ word, start, end, probability }]`. Populated only when `timestamp_granularities[]=word`.

ResponseObject.description: A response produced by the Responses API.

id.description: A unique identifier for the response.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the response was created.

model.description: The model that produced the response.

output.description: The output items. May contain `reasoning` blocks (reasoning models) followed by a `message` block with the reply text in `content[].text`.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the images were created.

data.description: The generated images. Each item has a `url` (default) or a `b64_json` payload, depending on `response_format`.

url.description: A temporary URL to the image, valid ~60 minutes. Returned when `response_format` is `url`.

b64_json.description: The base64-encoded image bytes. Returned when `response_format` is `b64_json`.

Completion.description: A completion for the provided prompt (legacy).

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the completion was created.

snippet.description: A short excerpt from the page.

content.description: The readable main text of the page. Present only when `fetch_content` was `true` and the fetch succeeded.

source.description: Which tier served this result: `primary` or `fallback`.

results.description: The ranked results, most relevant first.

cached.description: `true` when the results came from the short-lived (~15 min) exact-query cache.

id.description: Request id, echoed back in the response.

params.description: Method arguments. For `tools/call`: `name` (the tool) and `arguments` (its input).

result.description: Present on success. Shape depends on the method.

BadRequest.description: Invalid parameter. The body includes `param` with the offending field. Safety filter returns `content_policy_violation`.

Forbidden.description: Your tier lacks access to this endpoint (`tier_restricted`). Image generation requires `inference` membership.

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded: `rpm_limit` or `max_parallel_requests` (`rate_limit_exceeded`), or monthly quota exhausted (`quota_exceeded` / `insufficient_quota`).

PaymentRequired.description: The token allowance for the billing period is spent on a model that carries one, such as `glm5.2`. The request was refused before it reached the model, so nothing ran. Not retryable: the counter returns to zero when your billing period starts. The wire `code` is `cap_reached` or `monthly_cap_reached`.

error.message: Token allowance for this billing period exhausted for model glm5.2. The counter returns to zero when your next billing period starts.
